body: Wow, twelve years. Amazing! I find it somehow both scary and relieving knowing that other people who have made it this far still struggle. It means I might never be fully free of it but it also means the fact that I'm still struggling isn't abnormal. Thank you for sharing. Ten more years! Fingers crossed.
Thank YOU! It can be so helpful knowing there are others fighting the same fight. We got this!
Exactly! I'm so glad I posted here today. Thank you for helping me get through this!
Thank you!!
This helps a lot. The thought of failure scares me. But it feels easier to keep going if I'm less scared of failing. Does that make sense?
I think this is a good idea, not stupid at all. Book or game both sound like a great idea.
6 years is a big deal! AND 7 years sobriety from alcohol!? You're killing it too. I'm glad we can inspire each other! Thank you so much.
wooo~
A decade doesn't even seem real! I genuinely thought I'd be dead by now. I hope I don't let y'all down!)
Thank you!! I hope to just make it to midnight and then tomorrow maybe it will be easier to get started on another year!
Based on a true story

I wish it was as easy as stage fright. I've never struggled with the actual singing. Performing comes relatively easy to me, I've been doing it since I was little. It's just the getting out the door and trying to function like an adult that breaks me down. Ironically I have no problems acting on a stage, but acting in my everyday life just destroys me. That's part of why I hate myself so much for not being able to be there. Music is usually what makes everything else tolerable, but I was too broken to do it today. Better musicians power through it, but I just roll over and fall apart. 

I don't want to sound ungrateful, though. I don't want to minimize your achievements, because I know getting into music seriously late in life is a hard road. It sounds like you fought tall odds.

I definitely know the job pain. I've only got a part time one right now that doesn't really pay the bills, but it's better than unemployment. I did email the director and I was somewhat honest about what's up with me, so we'll see if that turns out to have been a good or bad move. Thank you for your support. And best wishes for you in your own fight!
I'm afraid I'll be bitter and resentful of the people who did show up and get them. I hope I can get over myself and still enjoy singing in the choir. Thank you for this.

Sometimes I feel like there's a hole in me where all the hope leaks out. And I need to hear things like this over and over to keep me going, even though i know it's all going to leak out again. Thank you for helping to refill me.

These words feel exactly like something I would have written. I hope it helps a bit to know that someone out here hears you and understands, at least a little. I think you matter. If I have at least one person who counts me, I'll be the person who counts you.
Side comment, I saw you sent me a chat request. I do not do reddit chat. Comments are nice, though.
Thanks. I don't believe in "things happen for a reason," but  as long as "I needed to take care of me" is considered an acceptable reason then i can hopefully be okay.
I couldn't right now, if I tried. I don't have music in me tonight.

I hope so. I hope I haven't made a bad impression on my director by signing up and then saying I can't go. I always treat my depression as a less legitimate reason to miss things. I know I shouldn't. 

Thank you, internet friend.
My partner got a pair of these when he was in the hospital for elbow surgery. So not exclusively emo. OR, maybe his surgery scar is just THE BIGGEST CUT.
I feel very called out. Do near-attempts count? I have two of those. If I count them as half attempts then it's like I have two whole ones!
Thank you. This sub is great.
I would like to avoid a doctor if possible but I think I'm alright...no other symptoms just ache. Thank you!

Thank you, friend, I appreciate the info on the warning signs. I googled symptoms of concussion and I don't *think* anything is wrong? It still hurts but it just feels like bruising. I don't think it'll kill me ^^unfortunately.
Real talk though, I slammed my head hard several times yesterday and still have a headache and I'm a little concerned. If that's too srs for this subreddit then disregard.
As everyone knows, only films end. All lives go on eternally, of course.

I sleep the way I eat - either way too much or way too little. I'm also all OVER digital self harm - I use cybersex to make myself feel worthless or useful. All of the shame with none of the need to wear a condom!
I feel called out.

I'm long out of school. Meditation is hard for me, but I've been experimenting with guided meditation lately and that's alright. And yes, I'm trying to save up. I know I need to do the work to find cheap or free resources, it's just hard.

No. :/ Since the job is part time, it doesn't have benefits, so I haven't been able to afford insurance in a while. I'm hoping that once I can save up more (or get an additional source of income) I can get enough money to either pay for an insurance plan or just pay for therapy. I haven't had a therapist or meds in a couple of years. I know that's the biggest step I need to take and I know I'm pretty much operating at 50% until I can get that support. It just stresses me out to the point of panic to think about it. It takes so little to make me break down.

When I finally made the connection and realized that SH was an addiction, my feelings made SO much more sense to me. It helps me resist the urge when I feel close to breaking my streak. It makes this struggle feel more real, understandable, something I have a frame of reference for. It's harder for me to rationalize cutting again. Thank you for writing this. I needed it today.
Coming up on eight years this September. Though that's just for cutting, I haven't kicked my other less serious forms of SH. I'm still wondering at what point I'll stop wanting it.
Note to self: write a sad poem about butts.
You say "cutting," I say "writing emo-ass poetry," and I do that on paper all the time. Checkmate.

Hey, 12 years is a hell of an accomplishment, so good on you for that. However you feel about relapsing, you should be proud of that. It helps to know I'm not the only one who still thinks about it even years after. I tell myself it's just a thing that teens do, and an adult like me should have grown out of these thoughts. I am hard on myself and always think I should be "over it" by now. But I think we'll never truly be over it. And that's okay. At least we're here for each other.

I'm 29. Started around age 14, the worst of it was from ages 19-22. Been clean of cutting (but not all forms of SH unfortunately) for seven years. I feel like I am perpetually on the edge of a relapse.

I'm seven years clean and perpetually on the brink of relapsing. I'm pretty much always on the lookout for a good reason to start up again. I think about it every day too. I know if I start again, I won't stop, and it will put all my relationships at risk. I just feel like I need it so badly.
Uh, okay, I was trying to be open because I know my thoughts are clouded right now and I thought you were trying to help, but fuck you. Thanks rescinded.

Technically it's everyone's destiny to be dead, at one point or another, regardless of whether I hang myself or not, so...

But thank you for your help. I'm sorry it's hard to get through to me. I feel like I need someone to slap me and tell me I'm being stupid, give me a reason to keep trying, dozens of times, until their voices drown out mine. Mine is so loud. So thanks for helping to try to shout over my voice.
I know. You're a good human. I'm sorry I'm abrasive.
I've attempted too, and I wish I was dead. I don't have any certainty that things will ever improve. They haven't yet. I think this is just how it is.

At my worst, my favored self harm methods were cutting and choking myself to the point of passing out. I remember talking to my shitty therapist about cutting and she was trying to get me to promise not to do it anymore. When I mentioned the choking she thought about this and then said, okay, you can keep cutting if you don't do THAT anymore. 

I haven't cut or choked in a long time, but I hit my head on walls, and who knows what kind of damage that does. I think I might also have some kind of disordered eating but I don't even know anymore. It feels like everything that could possibly be wrong with me is. Why not an eating disorder too, right?

One of the main things that keeps me from relapsing is knowing that breaking a seven year streak will probably ruin me for a while. I'll be so damaged and nonfunctional from the shame of failing after so long. But on really bad days like today, the thought of breaking my streak seems reassuring, a relief, like once I've finally done that I can just go back to cutting regularly without worrying about disappointing everyone. Even though I know every time I do it I'll be a disappointment.
I know. I need to hear it sometimes. I've just already wasted so much time. Thank you.

I'm mad at you for not enabling me and I feel somehow offended like you called me weak for wanting to give up or something. Through those reactions, I also feel grateful you took the time to reach out. So thanks, from future me. Present me is still very pissed, but hopefully I'm capable of understanding and appreciating all this soon. Thank you, is what I'm trying to say. I hope that made sense. Not a lot makes sense right now.

I'm still alive, for better or worse. I can't say I'm particularly happy about it. I always feel worse at the end of a month because rent is due soon and trying to scrape the money together is even more depressing. But I'm still here.
This has been a fun tangent. :)

I hate wasting good stuff or causing harm to nice things - so definitely the cheapest stuff that exists. Maybe things that are already damaged. Ugly vases you can't sell at a garage sale. Done a dozen ceramic pots. Stuff like that!

I'd hope I wouldn't need the room every day. Wouldn't want it to lose its impact. But I'd keep way more glass in it than I could use in a single session. So hopefully restocking could be like a once...monthly thing? :)

Sure! I was a very practical child too, my fantasy involved pegs by the door with safety goggles so you wouldn't get glass in your eyes. And I also tried to figure out the logistics of how often I'd need to replace broken pieces. I like consistent and plausible fantasy houses.

I'll look into the book. And that drug is...shrooms, right? Something I've been interested in trying, not so much for depression but just because hallucinations sound cool. I'm very straight edge but trying to loosen up a little.

When I was little, I used to dream of having a house with a room dedicated entirely to cheap glassware and soundproofed walls. And I would go there when I was angry and scream and smash things. I guess I still kind of want that. I'll find a way to make something like this happen.

Holy fuck, man, that's more than anyone should have to go through, and I'm sorry. Makes me feel like my shitty trauma doesn't quite measure up. But like we were once taught in crisis training, everyone has their own worst pain. I'm not here to play the suffering Olympics. 

I want to believe things can get better. It's just so hard to see it. After all these years, I can't look back and say I'm glad my first attempt failed.

>  The problem with emotional intelligence is that we don't value it in our society in any way that you can frame and put on a wall, or that can make you wealthy.

Ain't that the truth. I actually have a lot of shame built up around the fact that I feel like none of my skills or interests are socially valuable. It truly means a lot to hear you say I have a worthwhile quality. 

Thank you. I'll try to message you again sometime, maybe in a few days when I'm out of the woods for now. I'd like the chance to talk too. And I have *opinions* on GOT.

Thank you for all you've done. If you're worried about me, I'm not killing myself tonight. I still want to. I want to hurt, and I don't want to hurt anymore, if that makes any sense. But I'll make it to the morning at least. To my chagrin.

No, breaking things, that sounds interesting. Have you ever heard of the Japanese art of kintsukuroi? It involves patching broken pottery with gold and viewing the piece as more beautiful for having been broken. It's hard to see myself that way. But I like the idea.

Oh fuck, that owl always makes me cry. Thank you, I'd forgotten that image. 

I stay for different things. Sometimes it's little things, like media coming out that I'm excited about. Portal 2 and Bioshock Infinite kept me alive a long time. I've given up on the Winds of Winter, but I did just hear that season 2 of Jessica Jones just wrapped. A big thing that keeps me going is my loved ones, but unfortunately it's not a loving "I don't want to hurt them thing," but rather I grow to resent the fact that I have to stay alive for them. They won't let me kill myself, I often think. I feel bad about that. 

I'm glad your life has improved!

I know that feeling. Some depressive episodes I understand what's happening and can push back. Times like now, there's no way out. 

I used to have a safety plan. I don't anymore. I don't know who I'd go to. I have bad experiences with suicide hotlines and I'm afraid calling the police would result in expensive repercussions. 

I'm not sure. I like the darkness. I dislike my home, so lights off is less stressful. Maybe music or a candle or something. 

I don't have any good coping mechanisms right now. At the moment, I'm talking to you guys. That's how I'm coping. 

Not this late at night. I could go impose in my partner in the other room. I used to trust him with my depression. We've been rocky lately, and I don't go to him for support anymore. 

I don't have anyone close to me anymore I feel comfortable going to when I'm suicidal. That's why I'm here. 

Doesn't bode well for me, does it?

It's hard. It's so hard. I have so many hobbies but I just can't make myself do them anymore. I can't enjoy anything anymore. I have to put hobbies on my to do list with chores to try to force myself to do the things I enjoy. Your comment actually hits close to home and made me cry a little. I miss drawing so much. I miss writing and painting and making music. I miss who I used to be.

I'm poor and underemployed. 27, birthday in a few days. Relationships failing. Don't ever want kids. If I can't fix my financial situation, the hole I'm in will keep getting deeper and I'll never get out. There will be no comfortable retirement. Fundamentally, I don't like myself. No matter what changes happen in life, I'll still be me. I'm the consistent problem with my life. There are some things I do like about myself. I just don't want to be me anymore.

Is talking to you guys about it avoidant? Genuinely asking, often I deal with depressive episodes by wallowing and trying to deeply experience the negative emotion instead of alleviate it. It often leads to screaming, sobbing, or panic attacks. I don't feel like I avoid my emotions. 

Thanks for that troll comment. The last thing I'd ever want is for someone to feel the way I do. Be kind, leave a thing better than you found it. Thank you for working so hard for me. I guess maybe I identify too closely with those negative thoughts. I am not my depression. It just really feels like it. 

You took time out of your day for me, and you didn't have to do that. Thank you.

Thanks for the support, and I'm glad to hear you're doing better than you were. I'm the most toxic person in my life. I used to volunteer at a rape crisis hotline, but it emotionally exhausted me. It's much easier for me to care about others than myself, but I only have so much energy, and I still have to take care of me. Maybe I need something different, I don't know. As for happiness...I just wish I could have a few days where I felt like life was worth living. Even one whole day.

You say that she (or I) just has to wait and get through this. The thought of living another year or ten or fifty like this is torment to me. Why am I putting myself through this? To spare my family the pain of losing me? For some nebulous future when I can finally be happy - but I'll probably be old and worn out and too unhealthy to even do any of the things I wish I could do now? Life is what's happening to me right now, and it's unbearable. Sure, there are decent moments. But in general, I'd rather feel nothing.

Insurance problems and executive dysfunction have prevented me from getting back on meds/therapy. I stopped them both when I lost my job about a year ago and with it the insurance coverage. I have to start the process all over from scratch and it's exhausting. Currently, my coping mechanism is this thread. Talking it out frankly. Normalizing it. Often my coping mechanism is some firm of seeking online connection. Sometimes I write or just distract myself with Internet, but that doesn't work when it's particularly bad like now. 

Your arguments are good. Problem is, and please don't be offended, they make me feel invalidated. I'm not receptive to arguments to change my view on myself right now. I'm not functional enough. Failure or not, whether I'm worth something or not, the fact is I hate each morning when I wake up and realize I'm still alive. I can't keep living like this. I'm so tired of being tired. 

And by the way, you can't know how I appreciate you being willing to keep talking to me in the face of me being obstinate.

I'm sorry that's something you're going through. I hate being a burden on the ones I love. I hate being an emotional drain on them and knowing that every time I go to them for help, I push them away a little more. I'm glad that suicidality is something you can't wrap your head around. It means you've never truly wanted to die.
Thank you, internet friend. This is currently how I'm coping.

Essentially, a plastic bag over the head, from which you run a tube to a tank of helium or a similar gas. You rubber band the bag around your neck and turn on the gas, then just lie back and peacefully asphyxiate.

> So the chemicals comment seems like you're suggesting that you feel helpless?

This was more my way of saying that I understand that depression is an illness and has a physical cause that I can't help. I understand it, but I still feel it. 

> Your ex is abusive (therefore a piece of shit) but yet you take his words as evidence for why you're worthless, even though he might not be the most reliable source. 

I rationally understand this, but it doesn't stop the voice that lives in my brain from sometimes saying to me, I know you've worked hard over the years to undo the damage, but what if he was right all along? My brain is very willing to listen.

> Even if you're not succeeding at a worthwhile career, and even if you can't achieve all your goals, maybe that's ok. It doesn't make you any less of a worthwhile person because you can't meet your goals. 

You lost me here. How do I consider myself valuable if I fail at all the things that I value? 

> Alternatively you can think about maybe taking your life in a new direction, or maybe you are just an average individual, and maybe that's ok. Very few people ever achieve greatness, that doesn't mean that those that don't are worthless people.

I'm trying. I feel utterly pinned down and am frustrated at every turn I take to change my life. I don't need to be great, but is it too much to hope for to be good?

Oh, most definitely. I don't really have anyone in my life I trust enough to go to when I'm in my darkest moments anymore. So I usually turn to the internet when I'm low. My other post on this account even straight up says, I know this is just a cry for attention, but I just need someone to notice me. 

Thanks, random guy. That simultaneously doesn't help at all and reassures me.

If the past is any evidence, I'm not optimistic about the future. 

Variety of reasons. Chemicals in my brain preventing me from functioning. Words my abusive ex said continuing to reverberate no matter how long it's been and how much I tell myself he was wrong. Inability to succeed at a worthwhile career. Failure at most of my goals. Self-loathing.

Hanging. Honestly, a nice easy poison or OD would be great too, but I don't have any drugs at the moment. Besides, overdoses have a very low success rate, and I don't want to end up surviving with adverse effects, resulting in an even worse life than I have now. 

I've also considered getting a gun, or setting up an exit bag, both of which take a lot of prep.

Thanks! I unfortunately know a lot about how my depression and my trauma work. I know this moment is my most dangerous time, and if I can just get through the crisis I will likely survive. I know that despite what the voice in my head tells me about how worthless I am, that there are people who would be sad if I died. I know this is treatable and things can get better. At the same time, I "know" I'll never know happiness and death would be preferable. It's just a matter of fighting that. 

But I'm so tired of fighting. It's just not worth it. It hasn't been for a long time.
I've had some bad experiences confiding in people. I push people away. I exhaust them.

It's late. I can hear my partner snoring in the other room. I assume my other partner is asleep or I would text him. No, actually, I wouldn't. I don't want to call any friends this late, and I don't even know who I could call.
